title: Metal composition of ambient PM2.5 influences severity of allergic airways disease in mice.
ehr_evidence: We collected ambient air PM2.5 samples on Teflon filters in 1999 in Zerbst... and in Hettstedt... We used a well-characterized mouse model of allergic airways disease induced by ovalbumin (OVA) antigen...
summary: Experimental study using an ovalbumin-sensitized mouse model to determine if PM2.5 composition influences allergic airway disease severity and links to prior human epidemiological findings.
key_findings: Hettstedt PM2.5 administered before challenge increased PenH 190% compared to baseline, while Zerbst PM2.5 and control filter extract increased PenH 120% and 44%, respectively.

Hettstedt PM2.5 administered to allergic mice before challenge caused a significant increase in Mch responsiveness 2 days after challenge compared to allergic mice exposed to Zerbst PM2.5 or control filter extract.

Particles from Hettstedt increased sensitization to OVA allergen, as determined by serum levels of OVA-specific IgE collected 2 days after OVA challenge, when administered at either the sensitization phase or the challenge phase.

Eosinophil numbers in allergic mice exposed to Hettstedt PM2.5 before challenge were significantly increased 3-fold compared with allergic mice exposed both to control filter extract and to Zerbst PM2.5.
Both Hettstedt and Zerbst PM2.5 administered before challenge in allergic mice caused similar significant increases in protein, LDH, and NAG in comparison to corresponding nonallergic groups.

Levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ) in allergic mice were increased 6- to 8-fold by exposure to either Hettstedt or Zerbst PM2.5 particles before challenge compared with control filter extract.
captured_features: BAL cytokines (IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-13, MIP-2, TNF-α, IFN-γ)
data_source_type: environmental monitoring and laboratory animal experiment
limitations: limited sample quantities restricted sensitization phase analysis to allergic mice only
insufficient mice at 7 days post-challenge prevented statistical analysis
animal model may not fully replicate human allergic disease
